context: Linked data visualization: force-directed network graph with a synchronized sortable table, showing community detection results across 5 communities of 100 nodes
first_impression: A polished, well-structured split-panel layout with intentional color palette and clear typographic hierarchy between header, table headings, and data rows
what_works: The Tol Bright colorblind-safe palette is applied consistently across the network hulls, node fills, table dots, and bar fills — creating genuine color coherence rather than arbitrary category mapping. The table typography shows real hierarchy: uppercase letter-spaced column headers at 0.72rem quieter than group headers, with monospace tabular numerics for the betweenness column.
what_doesnt: The community column redundantly repeats the colored dot and name for every row even though rows are already grouped under a colored community header — this is data-ink waste that clutters the rightmost column. The subtle background bar fills in the betweenness column (opacity 0.18) are barely perceptible at this size, failing to add meaningful visual encoding while adding complexity.
